sections.title: Level 2 Concept of Idioms and Phrases
sections.content: At Level 2, it is not enough to simply recognize idioms; it is also important to use them correctly in context. Questions may include filling in the blank with the correct idiom, correcting an incorrect idiom, or identifying the meaning of phrasal idioms.

sections.title: Contextual Usage (Fill in the Blank)
sections.content: Step 1: Read the entire sentence carefully. Step 2: Understand the situation or emotion expressed in the sentence (such as happiness, difficulty, secrecy, etc.). Step 3: Choose the idiom that best represents that situation. Step 4: Place it in the sentence to confirm that the meaning fits. Example: 'After working all night, he finally finished the project by burning the midnight oil.'

sections.title: Phrasal Idioms
sections.content: Phrasal idioms are expressions formed by combining a verb with a preposition or adverb, and their meanings are different from the literal meanings of the words. Step 1: Identify the verb phrase. Step 2: Recall its common usage. Step 3: Confirm the meaning using the context. Example: 'Give up' means to stop trying or to surrender.

sections.title: Sentence Improvement with Idioms
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the idiom used in the sentence. Step 2: Check whether the idiom is written in the correct form. Step 3: If any word is incorrect, identify the correct idiom. Step 4: Replace it and check whether the sentence now makes proper sense. Example: 'Burn the midnight lamp' is incorrect. The correct idiom is 'Burn the midnight oil', which means to work late at night.

sections.title: Understanding Idiom Context
sections.content: The meaning of many idioms depends on the situation in which they are used. Therefore, it is important to understand the idiom along with the complete meaning of the sentence.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Changing words within an idiom. 2. Confusing idioms that sound similar. 3. Choosing the meaning of an idiom without considering the context.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: At Level 2, using idioms correctly in context is essential. Understand the situation in fill-in-the-blank questions, recognize the real meanings of phrasal idioms, and correct incorrectly written idioms.

tricks.title: Context First Rule
tricks.explanation: In fill-in-the-blank questions, first understand the meaning of the sentence and then choose the idiom.
tricks.example: He finally let the cat out of the bag about the secret.

tricks.title: Verb + Preposition Memory
tricks.explanation: Many idioms are formed using a verb and a preposition with a different meaning.
tricks.example: Look after = to take care of.

tricks.title: Fixed Idiom Structure
tricks.explanation: Changing the words of an idiom makes it incorrect, so remember its correct form.

tricks.title: Situation Clue Trick
tricks.explanation: The situation in the sentence can help you guess the meaning of the idiom.
tricks.example: Spill the beans = reveal a secret.

tricks.title: Elimination Method
tricks.explanation: Remove idioms that clearly do not match the meaning to find the correct answer.
tricks.example: If someone 'calls it a day', it means to stop working.

tricks.title: Common Exam Idioms
tricks.explanation: Memorize idioms that frequently appear in competitive exams first.
tricks.example: Once in a blue moon = very rarely.

tricks.title: Sentence Fit Trick
tricks.explanation: Place the idiom in the sentence to see if the meaning fits naturally.
tricks.example: He was in hot water after the mistake.

tricks.title: Practice Usage Trick
tricks.explanation: Using idioms in your own sentences makes them easier to remember.
tricks.example: She finally gave up after many attempts.
